function: Multi-agent DQN selects per-layer transmit power levels, beam direction codewords and RF-chain-to-subarray switch states for dynamic sub-connected hybrid precoding, maximizing energy efficiency (p. 7-8).
system: THz downlink mMIMO-NOMA BS, two antenna layers, each with two subarrays and two RF chains, single-antenna users, 0.34 THz, 200 m cell, no RIS (p. 3, p. 8).
method: Multi-agent DQN reinforcement learning: one centrally trained DQN with shared replay memory, per-layer target DQNs, hidden layers 64 and 32; fuzzy c-means user clustering (p. 3, p. 9).
data_channel: Own Python simulation: LoS THz channel with molecular-absorption path loss, users random in a 200 m cell, AWGN -174 dBm/Hz; no 3GPP model or dataset (p. 3-4, p. 8).
test_conditions: Single simulated setup (two layers, two users per cluster, four users per layer, 37 dBm); Fig. 11 sweeps RF chains and transmit power; no separate test scenario (p. 8-10).
baselines: Non-learned only: random policy, greedy beamformer selection and full array gain (FCHP) scheme; no earlier or standard learned method is compared (p. 10).
metrics: Training loss, average reward, average spectral efficiency, energy efficiency (bps/Hz/W), EE deviation versus RF chains and power, fuzzy partitioning coefficient for clustering (p. 9-11).
complexity: none; only network sizes are given (39 inputs, hidden 64x32, 16 outputs) plus a qualitative claim of lower memory and computational overhead (p. 3, p. 9).
q1_support: p. 4: "denotes the line-of-sight (LoS) path loss that depends on the THz frequency f and distance d". The channel is a custom LoS THz simulator with molecular absorption; no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured channel is used.
q2_support: p. 10: "under different Nrf values is shown in Fig. 11". This is a sweep of RF chains and transmit power; the paper never states that a trained agent was tested in a scenario not used for training.
q3_support: p. 10: "compared with that of the random policy and the greedy approaches". Fig. 10 adds the full array gain scheme; all comparators are non-learned, and no earlier or standard learned method is compared.
q4_support: p. 3: "to decrease the computational overhead and memory usage". Qualitative claim only; no parameter count, FLOPs, complexity order or runtime is reported (Table I on p. 9 lists layer sizes).
q5_support: p. 3: "simulated in the Python environment". No code or data link is given, and no public dataset or measured data is used.
notes: Included as area 3: the DQN chooses power levels, beam codewords and junction switch states of a dynamic sub-connected hybrid precoder (p. 7-8). Title and DOI on p. 1 match. No RIS: RISs appear only in the related work (p. 2). All five criteria are 0; q3 is 0 because the random, greedy and full-array-gain comparators are all non-learned.
